question:
A 52-year-old male presents for his routine health maintenance visit in May. His medical history
includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and a right inguinal hernia repair 6 months ago. His
medications include metformin, sitagliptin, enalapril, and metoprolol. He received a zoster vaccine last
year and had a normal colonoscopy 7 years ago. He has an 18 pack-year smoking history and drinks
moderately on weekends. He is allergic to amoxicillin and resides in Seattle. He plans to travel to
Australia and New Zealand in two weeks for his 25th wedding anniversary. Physical examination and
vital signs are normal. What is the most appropriate preventive health recommendation at this time?
Answer Choices: (A) Malaria prophylaxis (B) Abdominal ultrasonography (C) Travel health insurance
(D) Yellow fever vaccination (E) Low-dose CT scan of the chest (F) Hepatitis A vaccination (G)
Influenza vaccine (H) Cardiac stress test (I) Smoking cessation counseling (J) Pneumococcal
vaccination
 A. Smoking cessation counseling
B. Abdominal ultrasonography
C. Cardiac stress test
D. Low-dose CT scan of the chest
E. Pneumococcal vaccination
F. Yellow fever vaccination
G. Malaria prophylaxis
H. Travel health insurance
I. Influenza vaccine
J. Hepatitis A vaccination
